# US-202: GraphSAGE on ASOS (benchmark B2) and the A4 customer embeddings

<!-- Generated by `python -m ml.gnn report --artifacts artifacts --doc docs/results/us-202-graphsage.md` from artifacts/eval/gnn/*.json and artifacts/eval/risk/metrics.json. Do not edit by hand: rerun the command. -->

A benchmark of the ASOS return-prediction task, never evidence about rings (spec US-202). The ASOS numbers are real data (McGowan et al. 2023, arXiv:2302.14096, OSF c793h, CC BY 4.0); the A4 numbers are synthetic (the generated store); the paper's numbers are quoted from its Table 1; every timing is measured on the machine named with it.

## ASOS: GraphSAGE against XGBoost and the paper

Quality numbers of the CPU run. Device cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz (4 logical CPUs, 4 threads); torch backend; torch 2.8.0+cpu. Data: every event. Origin: ASOS GraphReturns, McGowan et al. 2023, arXiv:2302.14096, OSF c793h, CC BY 4.0; split periods per the paper: train 2021-09-01..2021-10-31, test 2021-10-01..2021-11-30. Nature: real. Test split 2021-10-01..2021-11-30. Every model of a protocol is trained on the same events, validated on the same seeded 10% of the train split (early stopping, isotonic calibration, F1 threshold) and evaluated on the same test events (US-201 splits and populations, ADR-10).

### MOD-02 (paper protocol only)

GraphSAGE, protocol A (Paper protocol: features computed over the labelled window, not available at decision time), full test set: F1 0.7760 at 0.5 and 0.7865 at the validation threshold, against the spec's F1 >= 0.78 (paper 0.792): **pass** at the validation threshold, **FAIL** at 0.5. Protocol B is reported with no threshold (ADR-10). A protocol A number is never product performance (NFR-16).

### Protocol B: Decision-time protocol

Origin: ASOS GraphReturns, McGowan et al. 2023, arXiv:2302.14096, OSF c793h, CC BY 4.0; split periods per the paper: train 2021-09-01..2021-10-31, test 2021-10-01..2021-11-30. Nature: real. Test split 2021-10-01..2021-11-30. Thresholds maximise F1 on the validation split; cross-entropy in nats and ECE over ten equal-width bins on calibrated probabilities.

Variant nodes (27): `variant_sales_loo`, `avg_price_gbp`, `avg_discount`, `has_variant_features`, `variant_degree` and 22 product type and brand one-hot columns. ## A4: GraphSAGE customer embeddings on the synthetic store

Origin: ReturnRing GraphSAGE customer embeddings (ml.gnn, US-202, spec 8.3): link prediction on the customer-identifier graph, no label; encoder graphsage-link-prediction-v1@2026-07-01T00:00Z (cpu, torch); as of 2026-07-01..2026-10-01. Period 2019-05-10..2026-09-30. Nature: synthetic (the generated Navigli Fashion store). The encoder never reads the ground truth (rule 12) and sees the store known at each instant only (rule 7).

Encoder: 2 heterogeneous SAGE layers of 16 units, aggregator mean, dropout 0.2, trained by link prediction on the (account, identifier value) uses known at 2026-07-01T00:00:00+00:00: each epoch hides 20% of the uses and scores them against random values of the same kind; a fixed 10% is held out for early stopping. Inputs: `n_card_values`, `n_email_values`, `n_device_values`, `n_address_values`, `n_phone_values`, `n_ip_prefix_values`, `tenure_days`, `n_delivered_lines`, `withdrawal_return_share`, `has_delivered_lines`, `n_welcome_coupons_used` (accounts); `kind_index_0`, `kind_index_1`, `kind_index_2`, `kind_index_3`, `kind_index_4`, `kind_index_5`, `kind_weight`, `n_sharers` (identifier values). Graph at the last instant: 20,000 accounts, 123,578 values, 139,086 uses, 4,690 values shared by two accounts or more.

| Store | Encoder | Instants | Rows written | Epochs | Validation AUC (self-supervised task) | Training s | Inference s (all instants) | Device: hardware, backend, versions | Load before / after training | Period |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | graphsage-link-prediction-v1@2026-07-01T00:00Z (trained here) | 2026-07-01, 2026-08-01, 2026-09-01, 2026-10-01 | 77,703 | 300 (best 287) | 0.9479 | 147.34 | 0.786 | cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz (4 logical CPUs, 1 threads); torch backend; torch 2.8.0+cpu | 14.87 / 10.73 | date not recorded in the metrics file |

The AUC measures the self-supervised task (a held-out use against a random value of the same kind), not abuse detection; what the embeddings add to abuse detection is the A4 row below.

## Method and limitations

- Scope: a benchmark of the ASOS return-prediction task (spec US-202, B2). ASOS has no identifiers and no abuse label: nothing here is evidence about rings. Abuse is measured on the synthetic store only (A4 row, and docs/results/us-204-risk.md).
- Graph: one per ASOS split, customer and variant nodes, one undirected edge per event. GraphSAGE is inductive: trained on the train graph, applied to the test graph, as XGBoost uses the test split's node tables.
- Model (spec 8.1): one heterogeneous SAGE layer of 16 units per relation, dropout 0.2, Adam 0.01, a 2-layer MLP head (64 units) on the two node representations and the edge's own features; binary cross-entropy, mini-batches of 131,072 events with the node representations recomputed on the whole graph each step, early stopping after 5 epochs without a better validation loss, at most 60 epochs; isotonic calibration and the F1 threshold on the validation split, as for XGBoost. The aggregator is the mean (sparse product); the paper and spec 8.1 use max-pool, available with `--aggregator pool` and not measured here.
- Protocol B (decision time): no label travels along the graph. A node's return count holds the label of every edge of that node, so the nodes carry label-free features only (leave-one-out sales, degree, flags, product attributes), and the leave-one-out return counts of the event's own customer and variant enter the edge head per event (the 30 protocol B features of ml.propensity). Trained, calibrated and judged on the decision-time population (ADR-10 amendment 1).
- Protocol A (paper): the paper's node features, return rates and reason shares included, on the nodes; nothing on the edge. Forbidden features (gender, country, age) are absent from both (rule 6, ADR-11): the paper's country virtual nodes are not built.
- MLP row: the same head on the input node features, no message passing: what the graph adds over the same features. XGBoost row: ml.propensity's model of the protocol (US-201 code path) on the same rows.
- Paper: the paper's GNN trains on the events of variants with a return rate above 0.8 or below 0.2 only, and is evaluated on the full test set.
- Paper: the paper's graph adds virtual nodes for countries (a forbidden feature here, rule 6), products, product types, brands and top return reasons.
- Paper: the paper's node features are computed over the labelled window (ADR-10, protocol A).
- Determinism: seeded Python, NumPy and torch, deterministic algorithms requested (warn only); the CPU run repeats exactly, a GPU run may differ in the last digits.
- Timings are wall-clock on the machine named with each run, with its load average; a shared CPU makes them an upper bound.

## Reproduce

CPU (any machine with PyTorch; DGL optional):

```bash
pip install -r requirements/dev.txt -r infra/requirements-gnn-cpu.txt
make gnn-asos                # python -m ml.gnn asos --raw data/raw --out artifacts
make embeddings              # A4 embeddings of the main and OOD stores into data/
make risk                    # runs A4 when data/features/customer_embeddings exists
make gnn-results             # this file
```

MI300X droplet (trainer-graphsage image: rocm/dgl plus this code; DGL backend), in the order of infra/spikes/README.md, 'The GPU session':

```bash
make gnn-image               # build the trainer-graphsage image (pulls rocm/dgl)
make bench-b2 DEVICE=gpu     # B2: the asos job on the CPU and the MI300X, both
                             # artifacts/eval/gnn/us-202-asos-{cpu,gpu}.json
make embeddings-gpu          # encoder on the GPU, embeddings copied into data/
```

Then on the laptop, with the metrics files and the embeddings copied back: `make risk gnn-results` (the A4 row needs the ground truth, which stays on the laptop).

Tests: `python -m pytest -m torch` with PyTorch installed (skipped without it); on the droplet `make gnn-test-gpu` also compares the DGL and PyTorch layers on the GPU.
